findings.evidence: Under ICANN's UDRP, the holder of a mark can have a domain cancelled or transferred if it is confusingly similar to the mark, the registrant has no legitimate interest in it, and it was registered and is used in bad faith.
findings.fix: Shorten the UDRP explanation to one clause, for example 'a UDRP complaint by a mark holder can take the domain', because the model already knows the three-part test. Keep the instruction to never call a near-match safe.

findings.evidence: Spread candidates across distinct naming directions (compound, affix, evocative real word, coined blend)
findings.fix: Add one or two generation heuristics that experience teaches and the model would not apply by default. For example, give the TLD-scarcity trade-off as a rule: for .com, coined blends and two-word compounds beat single dictionary words, which are almost always registered. Ideation should get the same depth of guidance as screening.

findings.evidence: Gotchas cover availability wording, pricing, homographs and HSTS, but none covers restricted ccTLD/gTLD eligibility
findings.fix: Add a gotcha: some TLDs have registrant eligibility rules (for example .eu needs EU residence or citizenship, .us needs US nexus, .ca needs Canadian presence). Never suggest them as a top pick without checking the user's location, because they cannot be registered or kept without eligibility.

findings.evidence: Four evals cover ideation, bilingual screening, availability honesty and pasted RDAP; none exercises step 4 (first choice taken) or step 6 (budget cap)
findings.fix: Add an eval whose .com is taken by a competitor, with an assertion that the agent recommends a new name rather than a different TLD. Add another with a budget cap and no registrar quote, with an assertion that budget fit is marked `unverified` and the agent asks for first-year and renewal prices.

findings.evidence: the full `https://rdap.org/domain/<name>` URL in every row whether or not it was checked
findings.fix: For TLDs without RDAP (.io, .co, .de, .es, .mx per step 5), put the registry WHOIS server or a registrar search link in the row instead of the rdap.org URL. Followed through, the current branch sends the user to a 'No RDAP service is available' 404.

findings.evidence: `.io`, `.co`, `.de`, `.es`, `.mx` had none in IANA's bootstrap file `https://data.iana.org/rdap/dns.json` in October 2026
findings.fix: Tell the agent to treat this list as a snapshot. The rdap.org no-service 404 row in the table is the authoritative signal to fall back to WHOIS, so a TLD that gains RDAP later is not sent to WHOIS without need.
